references.title: Effect of DHA on proinflammatory cytokines including platelets activating factor (PAF) in preterm neonates

references.authors: Kamal NM, Awad HA, Badr OG, Hassan SM, Hashem HE, Ahmed WO
references.title: The effect of docosahexaenoic acid supplementation in preterm infants on the incidence of necrotizing enterocolitis and its correlation with the level of platelet activating factor

characteristics.name: Methods
characteristics.value:
Study design: 2 arm double-blind randomized controlled clinical trial

Country: Egypt

Setting: NICUs of Ain-Shams University Hospitals

Study dates: September 2017 to September 2020

characteristics.name: Participants
characteristics.value:
Total number: 80

Inclusion criteria: Preterm neonates with a gestational age of 32 weeks or less at birth, weight ≤ 1500 grams, and clinically stable to begin enteral feeding,

Exclusion criteria: Persistent bleeding at any level, receiving anticoagulant medication, persistent vomiting, or both gastrointestinal malformations or surgery and mother taking ω-3 supplements.

characteristics.name: Interventions
characteristics.value:
Control group description: Unclear; if none or physically matched solution as mentioned in clinicaltrials.gov

Intervention group description: DHA 100 mg for 10 days from onset of enteral feeds (details not available)

characteristics.name: Outcomes
characteristics.value:
Primary outcomes: Clinical and radiological signs of necrotizing enterocolitis

Secondary outcomes: Anthropometry, feeding intolerance, severity of illness, hematological indices
